title: Start with the experience someone wants.
intro: Knowing that you want an adventure is different from knowing which character to search for. Scenario-led discovery gives people another way in: choose a mood or situation, then explore the characters connected to it.

blocks.alt: Talkie scenario discovery with an experience prompt, emoji selectors and a central character carousel
blocks.caption: Scenario exploration adds an experience-led entry point above the familiar recommendations.

items.label: A REASON TO EXPLORE
items.title: Lead with a situation.
body: The scenario prompt and emoji choices introduce the kind of encounter a visitor can enter before asking them to choose an individual character.

items.label: A CHARACTER TO CHOOSE
items.title: Reveal the next action.
body: Card hover states expose the chat action when the visitor focuses on a character. The design notes specify the reveal, movement and timing.

items.label: A DIFFERENT WAY IN
items.title: Support browsing and searching.
body: Recommendations, category tags and a dedicated search surface support different levels of intent.

blocks.label: SEARCH EVOLUTION
blocks.title: Make search useful before the first keyword.
body: The search design combines a visible input with recommendations, topical tabs and tags. Someone who knows a character can search directly; someone who is still exploring can narrow the field visually.
The interaction design also includes loading, no-results and network-error states, so the experience has an answer when a query does not return characters.

figure.alt: Talkie search exploration page with a search field, recommendations, topical tabs and tags
figure.caption: Search design · Recommendations and categories provide alternatives to a blank input.
